title: Administrative interpreter step
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, $B$ a four-tape configuration, $q,q'$ control states, $T$ a Boolean table word with cursor $p\in\mathbb Z$, and $\sigma\colon\mathbb Z\to\{0,1,\mathrm{blank}\}$ a state tape with cursor $s\in\mathbb Z$. Suppose the stopped interpreter's transition at control $q$, on the input symbol read from $B$ and the four symbols read from the evaluation configuration determined by $(B,q,T,p,\sigma,s)$, is the administrative action with target control $q'$, table movement $d_t$, and state instruction $(w,d_s)$, where $d_t,d_s\in\{-1,0,1\}$ and $w$ is an optional state-tape write. Then one interpreter step gives the evaluation configuration with control $q'$, table cursor $p+d_t$, state cursor $s+d_s$, and state tape unchanged if no write is specified or updated at $s$ to the specified value otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean input word and four-tape base configuration
Boolean table and integer table cursor
Boolean-valued optional-symbol state tape and integer cursor
Transition at q on the base input symbol and evaluation-configuration work-tape reads equals the stated administrative action
Table and state movements are signs
replaced:
If, on the symbols read in an interpreter evaluation configuration, the
transition function of the stopped table interpreter returns the
administrative action with table move $d_t$, optional state-tape write, state
move $d_s$, and next control $q'$, then one machine step from that
configuration yields exactly the evaluation configuration with control $q'$,
table cursor shifted by $d_t$, and state tape and state cursor updated
accordingly.
